COVID-19: Dispelling Disinformation

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
President Ramaphosa has warned that false information about COVID-19 vaccines is putting lives at risk. So what sources can we trust, what is misleading and how do we tell the difference?

Unique Selling Point:
We help sort fact from fiction when it comes to COVID-19 information by getting experts to answer questions posed by Carte Blanche viewers

Summary:
As South Africa struggles under the weight of a 2nd deadly wave of COVID-19, a desperate public is also being confused by a spate of conspiracy theories.

These range from alleged miracle cures like Ivermectin to disinformation that sow seeds of doubt about COVID-19 vaccines. Amazingly, a recent public poll revealed that 52% of South Africans would not even take the vaccine if it were available to them. https://www.iol.co.za/personal-finance/insurance/52-of-south-africans-dont-want-covid-vaccine-despite-sa-securing-initial-batch-f45373f0-6199-46ab-8207-fb632706b8e5


Those who doubt the efficacy of the vaccine include Chief Justice Mogoeng Mogoeng (https://www.iol.co.za/pretoria-news/news/covid-19-charges-against-chief-justice-mogoeng-mogoeng-over-devil-666-anti-vaccine-stance-c3fa8c22-bb44-4887-9a03-350492a91044)

and amazingly, many primary health care givers: https://www.timeslive.co.za/sunday-times/news/2021-01-24-fear-of-the-vaccine-jab-infects-frontline-health-care-workers/

In this story we look at why there is such scepticism toward the vaccine. Where does it come from and how can it be countered?

How can we dispel the disinformation surrounding COVID-19 and get South Africans to trust science? https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2021-01-24-a-hesitant-nation-survey-shows-potential-acceptance-of-a-covid-19-vaccine-in-south-africa/

Press Release:


The COVID-19 Infodemic: Dispelling Disinformation
Disinformation, bad science and fake news have spiked to unprecedented levels as the globe has been battered by COVID-19 for over a year. The WHO coined the description: an infodemic. To a nation firmly in the grip of the second infection wave, facing the death of loved ones every day and a scarcity of vaccines as they become available, President Cyril Ramaphosa wrote in his regular open letter that “… (w)hen it comes to fighting a deadly pandemic like this, honesty and trust are just as valuable as any vaccine.” Committed to credible information from expert sources that can help viewers take the best decisions, Carte Blanche investigates how disinformation, a lack of transparency and fear can combine to fuel the pandemic. We take some of the most frequently asked questions to some of the country’s top scientists.
Producer: Julian Sun | Presenter: Derek Watts

Script:



INTRO: As COVID-19 continues to ravage the planet, it is clear that humanity is not just battling a once-in-century pandemic, it’s also fighting a virulent infodemic of fake news.

DEREK: As mis & disinformation overruns our social media newsfeeds and flood our personal whatsapp groups, it’s becoming harder to discern fact from fiction, undermining our trust in science at a time in which need it the most.

V/O: The glut of conspiracy theories around COVID-19 has skyrocketed since the start of the pandemic. Stuart Jones from the Centre for Analytics and Behavioural Change has been tracking some of the most outrageous.

Stuart outlining some of the most popular conspiracy theories: 5G causes COVID, Bill Gates wants to depopulate Africa, microchips will be injected if we get the vaccine, mark of the beast etc




DEREK: The development of a host of COVID-19 vaccines is one of the biggest scientific achievements in history, yet the speed of this has many people doubting their safety

V/O: Professor Narnia Bohler-Muller is the Co-principle investigator of the largest and most comprehensive survey of South African attitudes toward the vaccine.

67% of South Africans will be willing to take the vaccine

18% probably won’t or definitely will not, 15% are undecided

Education plays a role – people with tertiary education are more hesitant compared to those with less than a matric

Trust in government plays a role – this breaks down along racial lines

Interestingly not many people buy into conspiracy theories. Most are concerned about the safety and side effects of the vaccine.



V/O: With South Africa in the grip of a 2nd deadly wave of COVID-19, the arrival of the first batch of vaccines has generated huge public interest.

DEREK: We saw this first hand when we put a call out on Facebook for viewer questions about the vaccine and as you can see, we’ve been inundated with over 1400 comments.

V/O: To answer your questions, we turned to one South Africa’s top virologists Professor Barry Schoub.








Monique Kaiser
What are the common side effects?

Selwyn Lloyd
Are there any cells from an aborted fetus in the vaccine?

Mazisi Ntuthuka
Can I take different vaccines (Mordena, AstraZeneca and Johnson & Johnson Jansen) as an extra precaution?

Craig Andrew Pritchard
How come this vaccine has be developed so fast and HIV, Cancer, the common cold doesn’t have a vaccine?

Ismari Jaquire Truter
1. What will the implication of the vaccine be to patients that suffered from covid 19 and why should they by vaccinated if they recovered from it?

2. Immune compromised children will get very sick if they do get Covid 19. How can they assure me as parent that it will be to protect my child if he or she is already on immunoglobulin replacement therapy? Why should they be vaccinated?


V/O: With the first batch of Astra-Zeneca vaccine due to arrive in South Africa on Monday, the government announced plans to begin inoculating frontline health workers within the next 2 weeks.

Yet some nurses are wary as, Sibongiseni Delihlazo from the Democratic Nursing Organization of South Africa explains.

Sibongiseni on nurses wanting to have more information about the vaccine
V/O: The imminent vaccine rollout in South Africa should be cause for celebration. After a year of devastation, at long last there is a light at the end of the tunnel. But doubts remain and disinformation continues to run rife. So what can be done?

Barry Schoub on trusting credible sources and believing in Science

Staurt Jones on what can be done when a family member believes in a conspiracy theory

And advice on what news to believe and what to discard
